title: AgriConnect and Djibouti: Creating jobs and boosting food security in a resource-constrained region
gist: World Bank Group's AgriConnect approach, piloted in Djibouti's first-in-region Compact, targets livestock, horticulture and dates to cut a 90% food import dependence and create jobs, needing US$185-245 million by 2030.

insights.claim: One in six people in the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan region faces food insecurity and 42 percent cannot afford a healthy diet.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Sizes the structural demand for food-system investment in the region.

insights.claim: Food demand in the MENAAP region is projected to rise 67 percent by 2050 while climate change, water scarcity and conflict constrain production.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Widening supply gap implies rising import dependence and a case for agrifood capex.

insights.claim: The agrifood sector already supports 63 million jobs in MENAAP, nearly three in ten workers, and could generate millions more via value chains beyond primary production.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Jobs framing links agri investment to employment-driven policy priorities.

insights.claim: Djibouti imports 90 percent of its food, with 16 percent of the population in acute food insecurity in 2026 and a share expected to reach 25 percent by year-end; unemployment is 39 percent.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Extreme import dependence and joblessness make Djibouti a stress case for food security policy.

insights.claim: Livestock accounts for three-quarters of Djibouti's agricultural GDP, and the Port of Djibouti livestock terminal handled over 1.2 million animals in 2024 while running below 20 percent of capacity.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Underused terminal capacity points to upside in Gulf re-export trade and processing.

insights.claim: Local horticulture meets only 10 percent of Djibouti's demand, vegetable imports exceeded US$35 million in 2021, and greenhouse tomato yields can reach 300 tons per hectare versus 40 in open fields.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Greenhouse import substitution is the nearest-term commercial opportunity.

insights.claim: Djibouti produces about 110 tons of dates a year while importing roughly 2,300 tons; the plan is to reach 5,850 tons after 2030 to cut the import gap and become an exporter.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Small base, but a clear import-substitution target.

insights.claim: AgriConnect addresses value-chain constraints together, aligning shared infrastructure with reforms to land, licensing, certification, skills and finance, rather than treating each separately.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Bundled infrastructure-plus-reform packages are the template likely to be replicated across the region.

insights.claim: An estimated US$185-245 million is needed across Djibouti's three value chains by 2030, targeting 10,000 farmers and pastoralists and at least 5,000 jobs created or improved.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Defines the financing envelope open to private and development capital.

insights.claim: Nearly three-quarters of Djiboutian households lack banking access and lenders view agriculture as inherently risky, constraining credit to the sector.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Credit scarcity is a binding constraint; collateral and leasing reform is a lever.

insights.claim: IFC is advising Tiryaki Agro, Turkiye's largest agri-food exporter, on a grain storage facility at the Port of Djibouti and working with the Central Bank of Djibouti on movable collateral registry and leasing reform.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Shows concrete private-sector entry points in Djibouti logistics and finance.

insights.claim: World Bank-supported projects report results across the region: Afghanistan 15 agri-SMEs and over 1,000 jobs; Morocco 730 producers; Pakistan Punjab irrigation reaching over 100,000 farmers; Yemen fisheries supporting nearly 4,000 fishers and over 11,000 jobs.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Evidence base used to justify scaling the AgriConnect approach.

insights.claim: Raising production alone is not enough; farmers need markets, businesses need infrastructure and finance, investors need predictable policies, and countries need resilient trade and water management.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Signals policy emphasis on market linkages and enabling environment over output targets.
insights.quote: The lesson is clear: raising production alone is not enough.
